expertNote.title: Selling on Amazon in the EU forces per-country VAT registration

expertNote.title: Masked email relays survive only when mixed with non-private addresses
expertNote.summary: Explains why iCloud+ keeping Hide My Email addresses on icloud.com matters: private relays get blocked unless the addresses share a domain and format with many non-private ones, a pattern otherwise only offered by Fastmail; unique addresses on your own domain are trivially clusterable.

evidenceSpans.text: Private email relays often get blocked, the only lasting solution is to put them on the same domain as, and in the same format as, a significant number of non-private email addresses.
As far as I’m aware the only other provider doing this is Fastmail.
You can make arbitrary email addresses at your own domain, but anybody who feels like it can trivially automatically detect that those are all you.

expertNote.title: Persistent polite escalation got three apps working on GrapheneOS

expertNote.title: A 99.9%-correct system with humans on the edge beats chasing 100%
expertNote.summary: Operational design argument illustrated by the UK eVisa failure: software always has bugs, so the resilient design is a mostly-correct process plus staffed escalation with agency to resolve edge cases on the spot, rather than a fictional 100%-correct system, which costs more than the residual-error plus humans option.

evidenceSpans.text: What is broken here is that it is possible to get stuck in an airport with no possibility of escalating sensibly to a chain of human beings with agency to resolve it.
Instead, we demand a 100% correct system, and save money on actually having people around who can deal with the edge cases and make sure everyone has a good time.
getting a project from 99.9% to 100% costs a lot of money, because that includes literally all edge cases ever

expertNote.title: Full-text search beats embeddings for most large-scale RAG retrieval
expertNote.summary: From large-scale RAG experience: full-text search is easy, portable, scalable and covers the 80/20, while embeddings need constant re-embedding, reranking, and vector-search operational burden; a long keyword query is painful but works for all use cases and is easier to maintain.

evidenceSpans.text: people vastly underestimate full text search and vastly overestimate embeddings. FTS is really easy, portable and scalable and gets you very far, the 80/20 rule applies.

You will inevitably end up having to re-embed more or different chunks of your text to accommodate more and more precise embedding search - at which point you’ll go the last mile and do reranking etc etc all the while having to support the operational burden of vector search.
you turn around and build a search query with 500 keywords and sure it’s painful but it just works, accommodates all use cases, scales and is overall less annoying to maintain.
